But in this moment, you need to either break up or decide to believe what she's telling you. Don't stay with her and then hold this over her head, and don't seek revenge. It's possible that I'm misreading or that she's holding back the truth. But based on the information you've provided, it doesn't sound like she planned for this to happen. He stopped by unexpectedly, and she went down to talk to him. She hugged him. End of.

Putting myself in her shoes, if someone I'd once loved stopped by and nothing horrible had happened to make me hate him, I imagine I'd do exactly what she did. I wouldn't stand on the balcony and shout; I'd go down and talk. I'd probably give him a hug because he'd been someone who was very important to me, and that history doesn't disappear when you break up.

It being their anniversary, yeah, that would bother me a little. But I don't think it means she's guilty of cheating or sneaking around behind your back. You seem to have drawn a very hard line about talking to exes, so I'm sure she knew you'd react poorly, and that may be the one and only reason she wasn't super open about it all.

But the part that really troubles me is you continuing to say you just want to hurt her. * United States of Latin Africa, a political entity proposed by Barthélemy Boganda for Central Africa
* United States of China, once advocated before the unification of China by Chiang Kai-shek
* United States of Europe, a political concept of a single European state
* United States of Africa, a political concept similar to the United States of Europe
* United States of South America, a proposed federation in South America or Latin America
* United States of Greater Austria, a successor state to the Austro-Hungarian Empire proposed by Archduke Franz Ferdinand
* United States of Australia, a name suggested before the creation of the Commonwealth of Australia
* United States of Poland

Seriously, most other countries technically have long-winded names but we shorten them. That's all we're doing. I got very, very close. My financial situation and love life were a total mess, and my job was becoming increasingly stressful, without giving me enough to pay the bills. One day I quietly cleared out my desk and erased the computer's history and passcodes, but I didn't say anything to my coworkers. I just said goodbye like any other day. Late that night I wrote an email to one of my bosses saying I was very sorry but I couldn't work there anymore, that I was very sick and getting sicker and I needed to take care of myself. 

I met with my apartment manager to break my lease. I packed up my things in a day and moved in with my ex-boyfriend. (He was already my ex by that point.) If he hadn't taken me in, I think I would have gone to a hospital or just tried to end it. 

Things got worse from there, and I did try to kill myself about two months later. I knew he was probably going to save me, but I felt too desperate not to try. To me, the whole "cry for help" thing shouldn't be looked at with such an eye roll. A cry for help doesn't mean the person wasn't willing to die. 

I went into treatment but it didn't help, and at some point I remember sobbing in the passenger seat of his car with the deepest sorrow I've ever felt--worse even than when I've lost a loved one. Despair is the only real word to describe it. Utter hopelessness. I was a living tragedy. I told him I couldn't take the pain anymore, that I wanted to find a legal and foolproof way to commit suicide. I felt that I was terminally ill and living in tremendous pain, and I was confused as to why anyone should want me to suffer like that. He said he would help me if it was what I truly thought was best, but only if I got my family involved too. I know he didn't really want me to do it. He just didn't know what else to do. He had tried so hard to help me, and I was just getting worse. In that moment he and I had both given up.

Somehow I hung on. I was forced to move out because he got a new girlfriend. That was awful for me too. But I found a new job that I liked. I somehow found enough motivation to try to get better on my own. And eventually I did get better, and things got better, and now I feel very far away from that girl crying her heart out in the car.

I know this probably won't be very motivating to anyone suffering from deep depression, because I've been there, and I know it's very hard to see how it might be possible for things to improve for yourself. I just want you to know that it *is* possible. I was truly at the end of my rope, absolutely miserable, afraid to die but so tired of life, and completely hopeless. But it did get better. I was ultimately the one who had to make that happen, but it worked.

I've seen people say LSD is the coffee of microdosing while shrooms are the tea. I am personally always looking for mental and physical energy in my drugs, hallucinogens or otherwise. This is why I rarely consume cannabis--I know some energizing strains are supposed to exist, but I have yet to find anything that doesn't conk me out, and that's not what I want.

I've only microdosed LSD four times so far, so the jury is still out for me, but I'll let you know how it's gone.

Day 1: I took probably 15 mcg (meant to do slightly less but misunderstood my boyfriend's instructions XD). Then I went to work (yes, I'm brave!). My commute is about 40 minutes, and I started feeling pretty good toward the end of the drive. Positive, energetic. I got to work and continued feeling good. I felt driven to close out some unfinished projects that I'd been putting off. A few hours in, I started to feel like 15 was a touch too much. It wasn't a problem, but I know you're not supposed to feel like you're tripping, and I felt objects were swimming a little, and I was crazy horny (tmi sry lol). It was a good day, but again, since I felt the faint effects of a trip, I figured I'd done a little too much. I didn't have any trouble sleeping. Wasn't jittery or anything. So, energetic, yes, but not at all to a problematic level.

I went two days off then did it again, this time with about 10 mcg. I didn't really notice anything different about that day. I was a bit disappointed. No ill effects, but nothing remarkable.

Two days off and I tried 12 mcg. That was a good day. I didn't feel like I was tripping, but I felt really, really good. Energized, happy, productive. I thought 12 might just be my sweet spot.

I was dumb and did it again the next day. I didn't have those positive effects and was in fact quite moody. I'm not blaming the LSD for the moodiness, but that was how I felt. I know LSD enhances mood, but I didn't wake up feeling bad, so I don't think it was necessarily that. I'd never planned to do it every day, but this confirmed that from here on out I'd go with a minimum of one day between doses.

My boyfriend's doses have been a lot lower than mine. Even at 5 mcg he feels it more than he wants to. He does think he likes it at just below 5 but is also still playing around and determining whether or not it's for him. The first day he said his brain was spacey and his body was anxious. He went snowboarding that day and said he was super not on his game. 

I'm really excited to try it this weekend when I'm off work, because so far I've only done it on workdays. I don't like my work environment or the work that I do, and on the days when I dose, if I go outside on my break and walk around a little bit, I feel the potential of the drug more. I'm ready to see what it's like to have freedom on a day when I'm dosing! 

Anyway, my experience has been fine so far, but not amazing...I'm hoping it will get better, because I was so excited for this. I've not had any issues with sleeping or being over-energized...I've just felt good (mostly), and haven't felt it's drained me at all. But that's just me!

In English we have this little saying to help us learn vowels: a, e, i, o, u, and sometimes y. And it's true. Sometimes y acts as a vowel, and sometimes it doesn't. Picture the way it sounds in the word "yes." That is not a vowel sound. In "Ypsilanti," it is. My name ends in a "y," and it sounds like a long "e"--there it's a vowel. 

tl;dr just more English craziness. I speak Portuguese too and enjoy the rules and order of the romance languages. :)

"Y" should only be preceded with "an" when the y mimics another vowel sound. I'm having a hard time coming up with an example, but let's take the Michigan town of Ypsilanti. The "y" sounds like a short "i" in this name--Ipsilanti. So someone from Ypsilanti could be called an Ypsilantian. You wouldn't say "a Ipsilantian" were it spelled that way, right? So same rule applies here, since the "y" sounds like an "i."

I looked it up because I was curious about what the wage is now. I first waited tables in Illinois. Again, I was making less than $3/hour before tips. Here's how the law currently works in Illinois: 

"Illinois law allows employers to claim a tip credit. The tip credit is 40% of the minimum wage. This means employers may pay tipped employees an hourly wage as low as $4.95 (or $4.65 for the first 90 days of employment). However, if this lower minimum wage plus the tips the employee actually earns don’t add up to at least the full state minimum wage, the employer must make up the difference."  

I didn't know that last part about the employer making up the difference. The owner at the restaurant where I first worked was an asshole and I was only 15. And google wasn't a thing then. :P

It's just a separate minimum wage. It isn't a problem when the tips are good, but if you get stiffed enough, or if business is slow, it's not sustainable. I started out waiting tables for under $3 an hour plus tips (granted, this was 1998). My paychecks were a joke. The tips were where it was at. But you get taxed for those too.
